page: Microsoft Azure F1amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a single dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor core based on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. This single-core configuration is paired with 8.0 GB of system memory and a local 118 GB NVMe SSD, with support for premium storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities due to the single vCPU limitation. Single-core CPU performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core CPU benchmarks, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations fall into the weak category. Large-block memory read and write bandwidths perform at average levels, while static web serving throughput is poor, placing in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high-frequency dedicated CPU core and a generous memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, alongside fast local NVMe storage. However, the single-core constraint limits its utility for parallel processing or high-throughput database workloads. It is best suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded tasks, lightweight caching, or development workloads that benefit from high clock speeds but do not require multi-threaded scaling.
